records.name: Haitian-American United for Change
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps new immigrants, especially Haitian Americans, with English instruction, job search and business startup help, and immigration referrals.
records.what_you_do: Ask for help with English instruction, job search, or starting a business, or ask for a referral on an immigration question. Staff also help clients with appointments and essential services, and the group promotes Haitian culture.

cost.text: Fees and eligibility are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Call (215) 681-8243 and ask about English instruction, job search, or business startup help.
first_step.basis: The group serves new immigrants, but the site gives no intake steps, hours, or eligibility rules, so the way in is unclear.
first_visit_tips: Call before you go: the site lists no office hours, and the address on record is the group's IRS mailing address.
If you prefer writing, the contact page has a form, and the site also lists the email jdafils@yahoo.com.

records.notes: No office address, hours, walk-in policy, eligibility rules, or fees appear on the site, so no what_to_expect was written. Tier 1 listed the IRS mailing address twice in two spellings; merged to one. The homepage mentions an immigrant holiday party with no year. The 2026 footer is a copyright year, not evidence. Status stays probably_active with low confidence.

records.name: Holmesburg Amateur Radio Club
records.summary: A ham radio club that meets monthly, runs a weekly radio net, and supports public service radio work for the Philadelphia area.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly meeting (visitors are welcome), check into the Thursday evening radio net, or ask the club for radio support at a public event.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the third Wednesday at 7:30 pm. Weekly net on Thursdays at 8 pm on 146.685 MHz (PL 146.2). No meeting in June or July.

cost.text: Meetings and the Thursday net are free. Membership dues are $20 for a full member, and $5 for each family member after the first full member. Associate membership, for people without a license, is $5. The site does not say how often dues are paid.

first_step.how: Email wm3pen@arrl.net to ask where the next meeting is held, then come to the third Wednesday meeting at 7:30 pm.
first_step.basis: The site says meetings are open to anyone interested in learning about amateur radio, and it lists a membership form and an email address.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings are open to anyone interested in amateur radio, and visitors are welcome. The site does not say how long a meeting runs or where it meets in person, so ask first. The Thursday net is a radio gathering where participants bring questions, news, and stories from their hobby.
first_visit_tips: The site gives only a mailing address, so email before you go to confirm the meeting place.
The homepage has noted months with a restaurant meeting or a Zoom meeting, so check it first.
Full and family members must hold an amateur license. Associate membership ($5) is open to people without one.
To join, print the membership form from the club's membership page and bring it to a meeting or mail it to the club.

records.notes: The regular meeting place is not on the site. The homepage mentions one restaurant meeting and one Zoom meeting; those one-off notes are left out of schedule. Net check-in rules are not stated. Dues carry no year. Dated pages: membership page May 2025, club info page January 2026, homepage July 2026 (newest). Net details come from austinseraphin.net, which the club links for its net. Newcomer rating raised from 3 to 4 because the site says meetings are for anyone interested in learning about amateur radio.

records.name: IAmShe
records.summary: A nonprofit that encourages women going through life changes. It runs virtual gatherings and empowerment events, and offers one-on-one and group coaching.
records.what_you_do: Join a Single By Design virtual gathering on Zoom (held every third Thursday), attend an empowerment event, or ask about one-on-one or group coaching.

schedule.text: Single By Design virtual gathering on Zoom every third Thursday of the month.

cost.text: Prices are not listed on the events pages.

first_step.how: Email info@iamshenikita.org or call 215-839-8165 to ask for the next Single By Design date, since registration for the August 2025 gathering was closed.
first_step.basis: Events have a Details link or a registration step, and the site gives an email and a phone number, so the way in is clear. The August 2025 page says the gathering is for women going through relationship changes, such as divorce, widowhood, or separation.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Single By Design gathering is on Zoom, starts at 7:30 pm, and runs every third Thursday of the month. The August 2025 page describes personal stories and lessons from other women's experiences of relationship change, with support and encouragement. The site does not say how long it lasts or whether it costs anything.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email or phone before the date, because the page does not state a time zone.
You need a computer or phone with internet to join the Zoom gathering.
Check the events page for the next date, since past gatherings show registration as closed.

records.notes: The events page lists six events. Only the August 21, 2025 Single By Design page gives a full date, so last_sign_of_life is 2025-08. Other events show only a weekday and day, and no years were assigned. The Single By Design page shows a 7:30 pm start with no time zone. The contact page also prints 215.613.7604 in its form section (not recorded). The aka is dropped from the record; the about page gives the legal name I Am Someone He Empowered, Inc. Two tier 1 address rows are merged to one. Hub of Hope is named as a co-presenter (leads_only).

records.name: Kidz in Da Hood
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that mentors young people, runs after-school enrichment, and helps families in need through community outreach. It also runs First Teachers, a parent support community.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for youth mentorship (including The Bloom Project), Kidz Corner play stations, or First Teachers through the Register Now form. You can also volunteer, which requires a background check, or call to ask about a start date.

cost.text: The site lists no program fees. Donations are taken through a Zeffy form on the site.

first_step.how: Fill in the Register Now form on kidzindahood.org for the program you want, or call 267-768-7738 to ask when sessions start.
first_step.basis: Joining means filling in a registration form, and the site gives no schedule, age range, start date, or description of a session, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a session lasts, where it meets, or what a session looks like. Mentoring is described as one-on-one guidance plus group sessions. Kidz Corner play stations run in small groups of 6 to 8 children at community events, with licensed caregivers and trained parent volunteers. Ask about start dates before you plan around a program.
first_visit_tips: Ask by phone or email about start dates and where sessions meet, because the site does not list them.
Volunteers must complete a state background check at epatch.pa.gov and upload it on the volunteer form.
The contact form has a menu that lets you pick Volunteer, Registration, Sponsorship, or General.

records.notes: The events page reads 'No events at the moment.' The newest dated item is a 2023 milestone on the about page, and the site's own wording runs 2023 to present. No later dated item was found, so status stays probably_active with low confidence. The homepage lists an after-school enrichment program that the programs page does not; both are recorded as the site's claims. The tier 1 address is the IRS mailing address, not a confirmed program site. The background check applies to volunteers, per the get-involved page.

records.name: Legacys Outreach
records.summary: A community nonprofit that offers family events, childcare, life skills and job readiness help, and referrals for health and mental health care. Its website lists these services without dates or costs, and its education classes are listed as coming soon.
records.what_you_do: Apply for services through the online form on the website, or attend a community event. The group also trains community members and childcare professionals. Its ESL, tutoring, GED, school age, and summer programs are listed as coming soon.

cost.text: The site lists no costs for services or events.

first_step.how: Fill in the Apply form at legacysoutreach.com with your name, email, and phone, and say which services you need.
first_step.basis: Services start with a web application, and the site does not say what the application involves or how long it takes to hear back.
first_step.what_to_expect: The form asks for your name, email, and phone number, plus an optional question about the services you need. A staff member says they will reach out to collect the information they need. The site does not say how long that takes, whether there are documents or fees, or what a visit looks like.
first_visit_tips: Have your name, email, and phone number ready for the online form.
The site lists no office hours, so call (215) 839-6898 before you go to the office.
The ESL, tutoring, GED, school age, and summer programs are marked coming soon, so ask before planning around them.

records.notes: The programs page lists five programs marked coming soon, with placeholder text, so they are not recorded as running. The event page gives no date, so no dated evidence was found. The founding year is not stated. The homepage's tree-planting figure is not explained on the site and is not used. The contact page appears to print the state as AP; recorded here as PA with the same ZIP code. Tier 1 address lacked Suite 105.

records.name: Mayfair Business Improvement District (BID)
records.summary: The business improvement district for the Mayfair shopping streets along Frankford, Cottman, Ryan, and Robbins Avenues. Commercial property owners fund it, and it runs public events such as the Third Thursday Night Market.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Third Thursday Night Market on Frankford and Cottman Avenues, sign up for the newsletter, or send a question through the contact form.

schedule.text: Third Thursday Night Market on Frankford and Cottman Avenues, 6 to 9:30 pm, on third Thursdays through the season.

first_step.how: Come to the Third Thursday Night Market at Frankford and Cottman Avenues, or sign up for the newsletter at mayfairphilly.com.
first_step.basis: The market is a public street event, and the site lists a newsletter sign-up and a contact form. It does not describe how residents take part in the organization itself.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists the Third Thursday Night Market as an evening event from 6 to 9:30 pm on Frankford and Cottman Avenues. It does not say what vendors or activities you will find there, or whether it is free. The district's own work is mostly about the shops: cleaning, public safety, marketing, and building improvements.
first_visit_tips: Check the site for the next market date, since the events list changes over time.
The site lists no office hours or public meetings, so call (267) 538-4668 before you visit the office at 2990 St. Vincent St, 2nd Floor.
If you want to attend a meeting, ask by email, since none are listed on the site.

records.notes: Scope call for the orchestrator: this is a business improvement district funded by commercial property owners. It is published because it runs public events, but its site lists no public meetings, membership, or volunteer route. Tier 1 said it hears zoning proposals; the group's own site never mentions zoning, so that was removed. The city list still shows it as a registered community organization (RCO 243), which comes from city data, not the group's site. The site's Thursday August 28 and Thursday September 18 items have no year and match 2025 by weekday, so they were not used as dated evidence. Status stays active from tier 1, based on the city registry date, which is not a group post; recheck it. Mayfair CDC is named as holding a board seat (leads_only). Tier 1's two location rows are merged.

records.name: Tacony CDC
records.summary: A neighborhood group that residents founded in 2001 to preserve Tacony's housing. It now works to revitalize Torresdale Avenue, the main shopping street, and runs events such as Tacony Third Thursdays and a yearly Halloween celebration.
records.what_you_do: Come to a Tacony Third Thursday event, join a seasonal street celebration, or contact the office about neighborhood services, business help, and what the area needs.

schedule.text: Tacony Third Thursdays runs every third Thursday of the month, 6 to 9 pm, at Costello Boxing Gym on Torresdale Avenue.

cost.text: The site does not list costs for the events or programs.

first_step.how: Go to Tacony Third Thursdays on the third Thursday of the month, 6 to 9 pm, at Costello Boxing Gym on Torresdale Avenue.
first_step.basis: The Third Thursday event is for the whole family and community, and the site gives its time and place. The site does not say how residents join the group or volunteer.
first_step.what_to_expect: Tacony Third Thursdays runs from 6 to 9 pm and is aimed at the whole family. The site lists a food truck, produce and flowers, live music, family activities, and tables from local organizations and elected officials. The site does not say whether it costs anything or whether you need to sign up.
first_visit_tips: You can come for part of the evening, since the event runs from 6 to 9 pm.
Call (267) 276-2586 before you go, because the site lists no office hours.
The site says to check the Tacony CDC Facebook page for current dates, so look there before you go.

records.notes: Office address conflict for the orchestrator to confirm: the group's contact page says 4823 Longshore Ave, #101, while the city NAC list (tier 1) says 4819 Longshore Ave, Unit C. The record uses the group's own page, and the city coordinates were dropped because they point to the older address. The site does not state legal status, so kind stays civic; it calls itself a neighborhood group and a community development corporation. The site's staff are Amarynth Ruch (Corridor Manager) and Gwen Thomas (NAC Program Coordinator); Xhulio Binjaku, the tier 1 contact, is not named on the site. Status is lowered from active to probably_active: the newest dated post on the group's blog is April 29, 2025, and the tier 1 active status rested on the city list date. The 'starting April 20th' note for Third Thursdays has no year and is left out. A search for a Tacony NAC meeting schedule found nothing usable, and an older office address from a search result was not used.
